Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list. Answers below (high level) — happy to dive deeper on the call and share more artifacts.

1) At‑rest key model
- Redwood supports envelope encryption with per‑customer data keys. For hosted customers we offer two patterns: 
  a) Redwood‑managed keys (default): root/master keys are managed by Redwood KMS; data keys are unique per‑tenant.
  b) Customer‑managed keys (CMK): customers can bring keys via cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS) with envelope encryption; we support customer rotation policies.
- Per‑customer envelope keys are available in both Hosted and Dedicated. HSM‑backed keys (FIPS/HSM) are available for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we support CMK via customer cloud KMS (where the KMS provider may be HSM‑backed depending on the provider tier).

2) HSM jurisdiction and attestation
- For Hosted: CMK via your AWS/GCP/Azure KMS will reside in the region you configure (we recommend provisioning the key in the same cloud region as your workload). Redwood does not export private key material.
- For Dedicated/Private: we can offer HSM‑backed root keys (HSM appliance or cloud HSM) and provide attestation statements where available. We can surface HSM certs/attestation evidence during procurement.

3) Audit logs and retention
- Default telemetry: request_id, timestamp (UTC), model_id, route, truncated_prompt_hash (SHA-256, first 64 bits), response_token_counts, actor_id.
- PII handling: we perform configurable redaction (configurable regex and tokenization) at ingestion; by default we redact full credit card numbers and SSNs patterns and truncate long free‑text fields unless you opt into collection.
- Retention: we can configure retention up to 3 years for enterprise plans; 365 days is supported and we will provide a sampling/configurable export. Attached CSV is a sample extract (fields and redaction columns).

4) In‑transit
- All production ingress/egress uses TLS 1.3. We support mTLS for dedicated endpoints and private deployments; for hosted API we support client certs via dedicated VPC peering or VPN + TLS (mutual TLS is supported when you provision a private endpoint).

5) Evidence and next steps
- We maintain SOC 2 Type II evidence and will share the compliance packet under an NDA (link below). We can also provide HSM attestation and key proof artifacts for Dedicated/Private engagements.

Recommended pilot approach (what has worked well):
- Pilot start: use customer CMK (cloud KMS) in us‑west to validate key separation and envelope encryption without needing HSM appliances.
- Parallel security deep‑dive: 45m call with your security + our security engineer to review logs, redaction configs, and attestations.
- SOW/Procurement: after the deep‑dive we can provide a scoped SOW and pricing for Dedicated HSM option if you want physical HSM later.

I attached the CMK/HSM options doc and a short audit log sample. For the deep‑dive call I can bring our security engineer (Karthik) and solutions architect (Jonas) — proposed windows Tued–Thu 10–12 PT.
